title: Ik haal je op
goal: Use object pronouns for people and things, and invite, accept, decline and make arrangements.

blocks.content: Ik haal je op
It is Monday 30 November. Sofia invites her friends to a housewarming at Kastanjestraat 14 on Saturday 12 December at 19.00.
In this lesson you will use object pronouns for people and things, invite people, and arrange who picks whom up and where.

content: , the object pronoun is bold, and time and place are

blocks.content: Story: the housewarming invitation
Sofia sends her invitation to Henk, Noor, Fleur, Daan, Lotte, Piotr, Kasia and Ahmed. Daan sees it at the office and answers.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Hoi Daan! Op zaterdag 12 december geef ik een housewarming. Kom je ook?

turns.speaker: Daan
turns.text: Ja, natuurlijk! Ik kom graag. Hoe laat begint het?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Om zeven uur, op Kastanjestraat 14. Ken je het adres?

turns.speaker: Daan
turns.text: Ja, ik ken het. Ik haal Lotte op en we komen samen.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Leuk! Ik nodig Piotr ook uit. Ken je hem?

turns.speaker: Daan
turns.text: Ja, ik ken hem van jouw Nederlandse les.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: En Noor en Fleur? Ik app ze straks.

turns.speaker: Daan
turns.text: Goed. Laat je het even weten? Dan app ik Lotte ook.

words.example: Ik kom graag naar je housewarming.

blocks.content: Object pronouns: people
An object pronoun replaces a person after the verb. You already know a few fixed chunks; now you can use the forms as a system.

children.content: Sofia belt me. / Sofia belt mij.
Ik haal je op. / Ik haal jou op.

words.example: Ik ken hem. De wijn? Ik neem hem mee.

words.note: Its object use for plural people is new here; ze as a subject is known from 14-a.

blocks.content: In an ordinary sentence, me, je and ze are light forms; mij, jou and haar carry more stress. U has the same form as a subject and an object.

props.translation: Daan is picking me up at six.
props.note: The object pronoun follows the finite verb and comes before the time.

props.translation: I’ll pick you up at the bus stop.
props.note: Jou is stressed here; je is also possible without emphasis.

props.translation: I’m inviting him too.
props.note: Hem replaces a male person. The separable prefix uit stays at the end.

props.translation: Daan is taking her home.
props.note: Haar replaces Lotte.

words.meaning: to bring; to take someone somewhere

props.translation: Henk is picking us up.
props.note: Ons is the object pronoun for wij/we.

props.translation: I’ll message you all later.
props.note: Jullie is both subject and object form.

props.translation: I’ll see them Saturday.
props.note: Ze is the object form for plural people.

blocks.content: Mij and jou are stressed forms; me and je are lighter. Ze is also a light form for her. After a preposition, use person forms such as met mij, voor jou, bij ons or zonder hem.

content: → Ik zie je / Ik zie jou. After a verb, use an object form, not the subject form jij.

blocks.content: After a preposition
After a preposition such as met, voor, bij or zonder, use the stressed person form. For a thing after a preposition, repeat the noun; do not use an er-form in this lesson.

props.translation: Piotr is coming with me and Kasia.
props.note: After met, use mij.

props.translation: Without her, I don’t know the address.
props.note: After zonder, use haar.

content: Zonder haar weet ik het adres niet.

blocks.content: For a housewarming, hosts usually give a clear date and start time. Guests plan social events in their agendas weeks ahead and arrive on time. At the door, a guest rings the bell (de bel) or rings (aanbellen).

words.note: This meaning is new; de bel = a bicycle bell in 16-b.

blocks.content: Object pronouns: things
The object pronoun for a thing follows the noun’s grammatical gender: hem for a de-word, het for a singular het-word, and ze for plural nouns.
A de-word → hem

children.content: De wijn? Ik neem hem mee.
De uitnodiging? Ik stuur hem vandaag.

blocks.content: A het-word → het

children.content: Het adres? Ik app het straks.

blocks.content: A plural noun → ze

children.content: The same ze works for plural people: Ik app ze straks.

blocks.content: For things: de-word → hem; het-word → het; plural → ze. The pronoun matches the noun’s gender, not the object itself.

props.translation: The wine? I’ll bring it along.
props.note: Wijn is a de-word, so the object pronoun is hem.

props.translation: The address? I’ll send it later.
props.note: Adres is a het-word, so use het.

props.translation: The flowers? Lotte is buying them.
props.note: Plural nouns use ze.

content.text: De wijn? Ik neem het mee.

content: → De wijn? Ik neem hem mee. A de-word takes hem as its object pronoun.

blocks.content: Where does the pronoun go?
Put the pronoun right after the finite verb, after the subject when the subject follows the verb. It stays before a time or place phrase and before a separable prefix at the end.

props.translation: I’ll pick you up at seven.
props.note: Pronoun after haal; time follows; separable prefix op is last.

props.translation: On Saturday I’ll pick you all up at the bus stop.
props.note: After a fronted time, the subject follows the finite verb; the pronoun follows the subject.

props.translation: Daan is taking her along.
props.note: The pronoun comes before the separable prefix mee.

props.translation: Can you help me?
props.note: After the finite verb kun, the subject je comes first in this question, then the object me.

blocks.content: In a main clause: subject + finite verb + object pronoun + time/place + separable prefix. With a fronted time: time + finite verb + subject + object pronoun + place + prefix.
Find the finite verb. Then put the person or thing after it. If the subject follows the verb, put the object after the subject.
Add time and place after the pronoun; keep a separable prefix at the end: Ik haal je om zes uur bij de halte op.
Inviting and arranging

Invite someone with uitnodigen. The verb separates: Ik nodig je uit. You can accept with Ik kom graag!, decline with Helaas kan ik niet., or ask for a reply. For things after a preposition, repeat the noun: Ik kom met de fiets.

props.translation: I’m inviting you to my housewarming.
props.note: The object pronoun comes between nodig and the prefix uit.

props.translation: Shall I pick you up?
props.note: With a modal, the object pronoun comes before the final separable infinitive ophalen.

props.translation: Just call me at the bus stop.
props.note: Recycles the imperative and chunk Bel me maar! (15-b).

props.translation: See you Saturday.
props.note: A familiar chunk; this lesson shows je as an object pronoun.

words.example: Tot zaterdag! Ik zie je zaterdag.
words.note: This chunk is known from 07-a; this lesson explains je as an object pronoun.

props.translation: I’m coming by bike.
props.note: Repeat the thing after met; no er-form yet.

blocks.content: Story: Sofia phones Piotr
Piotr and Kasia do not know Lombok well. Sofia offers to meet them at the bus stop.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Hoi Piotr! Ik app je over mijn housewarming.

turns.speaker: Piotr
turns.text: Hoi Sofia! Ja, Kasia en ik komen graag.

turns.speaker: Piotr
turns.text: Nee, stuur je het naar mij?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Ja, ik stuur het straks. Kastanjestraat 14.

turns.speaker: Piotr
turns.text: Dank je. Wij kennen Lombok niet goed.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Geen probleem. Ik haal jullie om half zeven op bij de bushalte.

turns.speaker: Piotr
turns.text: Dat is fijn. Bel je me bij de halte?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Ik bel je bij de bushalte. Ik kom met de fiets.

Replace the noun with an object pronoun

Daan is a man; use hem.
Plural people take ze; not hen/hun.
Wijn is a de-word, so use hem.
Adres is a het-word; use het.
Plural things take ze.
Two people are plural, so use ze.
Sofia is a woman; use haar.

items.note: Unstressed je is the normal lighter form.

items.prompt: Henk brengt **Sofia en Noor** naar huis.
items.note: Plural people: ze; do not use hen/hun.

blocks.content: Complete the invitation

data.instruction: Fill each blank with one word.

items.prompt: Sofia: Ik nodig … uit. / Daan: Leuk! Ik kom graag.
items.note: The object pronoun follows nodig and comes before the separable prefix uit.

items.prompt: Daan: Ik haal Lotte op. / Sofia: Ken je …?
items.note: Lotte is a woman; the object form is haar.

items.prompt: Sofia: Ik app Piotr en Kasia. / Daan: App … vanavond.
items.note: Plural people take ze.

items.prompt: Piotr: Stuur je het adres naar …? / Sofia: Ja, ik app het … .
items.note: After naar use stressed mij; straks is the time word.

items.prompt: Sofia: Zal ik … ophalen? / Piotr: Ja, graag!
items.note: Piotr and Kasia are jullie; after the modal phrase use the object before ophalen.

items.prompt: Noor: Kom je ook? / Ahmed: Helaas kan ik … .
items.note: A polite decline: Helaas kan ik niet.

blocks.content: Put the words in order

data.instruction: Put the words in order. Write the full sentence.

items.prompt: Put in order: haal / je / ik / morgen / op
items.note: Pronoun follows the finite verb and comes before time and prefix.

items.prompt: Put in order: zaterdag / jullie / haal / ik / bij de bushalte / op
authorsVersion: Zaterdag haal ik jullie bij de bushalte op.
items.note: Fronted time causes inversion; the object follows the subject.

items.prompt: Put in order: uit / nodig / hem / ik / ook
items.note: Object pronoun follows nodig; separable prefix uit is last.

items.prompt: Put in order: haar / Daan / neemt / mee
items.note: Object pronoun comes before the separable prefix mee.

items.prompt: Put in order: mij / stuur / je / het adres / naar
authorsVersion: Je stuurt het adres naar mij.
items.note: After naar use stressed mij. Keep the object noun before the prepositional phrase.

items.prompt: Put in order: je / haal / zal / ik / op / ?
items.note: Modal zal + subject ik + object je + infinitive ophalen.

items.prompt: Put in order: niet / ken / ik / hem
items.note: The object pronoun follows the verb; niet stays after the definite object pronoun.

data.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using the object pronoun.

items.note: Noor is a woman; her object pronoun is haar.
Piotr is a man; hem goes before uit.
Wijn is a de-word; use hem.
Adres is a het-word; use het.
Plural things take ze.

items.prompt: Ik zie jou zaterdag. (make the object unstressed)
items.note: Je is the unstressed form; jou is stressed.

items.note: Object pronoun after the finite verb; prefix op is at the end.
Hem replaces a male person; uit is the separable prefix.

items.note: Jullie is the object; the separable infinitive is ophalen.
Het adres is a het-word.
Haar replaces Lotte; mee is the prefix.
Fixed polite decline; no subordinate clause.

passage.title: De uitnodiging
passage.content:
Hoi allemaal!
Op zaterdag 12 december geef ik een housewarming. Het feest begint om 19.00 uur op Kastanjestraat 14. Kom je ook? Laat je het even weten?

Henk: Ik kom graag! Tot zaterdag.
Daan: Ja, natuurlijk! Ik haal Lotte op en we komen samen.
Lotte: Ja, graag! Daan haalt me op.
Noor: Ik kom graag! Fleur komt ook.
Piotr: Kasia en ik komen graag. We kennen Lombok niet goed.
Ahmed: Helaas kan ik niet. Dan ben ik bij mijn familie.

Sofia: Fijn! Ik haal Piotr en Kasia om half zeven op bij de bushalte. Ik app jullie het adres.
Tot zaterdag! Sofia

blocks.content: Summary
People: me/mij, je/jou, u, hem, ze/haar (her), ons, jullie, ze (them).
Things: de-word → hem; het-word → het; plural → ze.
Position: finite verb + subject (if present) + object pronoun; then time/place; separable prefix last.
After a preposition use stressed person forms: met mij, voor jou, bij ons. Repeat a thing noun after a preposition.
